cover_letter.greeting: Dear Lambda DC / Infrastructure Finance Team,
paragraphs: I'm applying for the Senior FP&A Analyst, Supply Chain Finance role at Lambda. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. What interests me is the link you draw between purchasing plans, delivery schedules and cash. For an AI cloud, the timing of equipment spend matters as much as the price, and idle equipment is cash tied up.

At Thomson Reuters I handled cash flow analysis and reconciliation across 80%+ of total inflows, and the order-to-cash work I supported cut the cash conversion cycle by 20%. At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%, and ran variance and sensitivity analyses on budget changes. In my MBA I modeled a 6-project, 35.4 MW solar portfolio, including DSCR, NPV and levered IRR.

That maps to the commitments tracking, the cash forecasting and the variance work in this role. I haven't worked in hardware supply chain finance, so supplier economics and depreciation by asset class would be new to me, and I'd plan to learn them quickly from Sourcing and Accounting. I'd bring careful reconciliation and clear explanations of what changed and why. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
